From factory to site

Built in a factory. Standing in a day.

  1. Two modules, made indoorsEach module is welded, closed in with Kingspan QuadCore panels, wired and plumbed in the factory, down to the furniture.
  2. Lined up on siteThe 2.1 m module travels as a normal load, the 3.1 m one as a permitted wide load. Footings are set before they arrive.
  3. Bolted into one homeA crane brings the modules together and the single joint bolts from inside: 9 bolts through the posts, 7 through the floor frame.
  4. Set on the footings, ready to live inPowerPanel solar is already on the roof and the 900 L tank sits in the floor. About one day from truck to keys.

Wheelchair version

The same two modules, set up so a wheelchair user can live here on their own.

Step-free way in

A 1 m wide door with a level threshold, and a 1:12 ramp or a platform lift up to the floor.

Room to turn

80 cm clear paths to everything and a 1.5 m turning circle in both the living area and the bathroom.

Bathroom that works

Roll-in shower with a level floor, grab bars beside the toilet, a wall-hung basin and a kitchen sink you can roll under.

Floor that opens up

A regular bed instead of the raised platform, a deeper bathroom, and overhead cabinets for the rest.

How it works

  1. Choose a planStart from a signature plan or a module kit. Every one is a complete, working home.
  2. Make it yoursMove rooms, doors and windows, pick finishes and size the solar and water. The checks tell you if anything doesn’t fit.
  3. Request a quoteSend your design in one step. You get a fixed price for your exact home, not a guess.
  4. Built and deliveredModules are made in the factory, trucked to your land and joined on screw piles in about a day.

What’s included

Steel frame that lasts

Bolted galvanized steel frame on screw piles, closed in with Kingspan QuadCore AWP panels over STEICO wood-fibre insulation. Walls reach U 0.15 or better. No concrete slab needed.

Its own power

About 3.5 to 4 kWp of Kingspan QuadCore PowerPanel solar for cold climates, a LiFePO4 battery and a hybrid inverter. An induction hob and DC fridge keep demand low.

Its own water

Rain runs through a first flush to an outside tank, then to a 900 L store inside the warm floor that never freezes, and through a filter and UV lamp. A composting toilet uses no water at all.

Fresh, warm air

Heat-recovery fresh air, an efficient heat pump and triple glazing. A sealed backup hearth is lit only in the coldest weeks.

Eleven layers, all bolted

Every layer comes off with a spanner, so the home can be moved, repaired or taken back to the factory for reuse.

  1. Roof panelsKingspan QuadCore PowerPanel with built-in solar, LEC core
  2. Roof frameSteel rafters on a bolted grid
  3. High windows and ceilingDaylight deep into the room, and a stack vent for summer nights
  4. Wall panelsKingspan QuadCore AWP with LEC core, the ONIS wall
  5. InsulationSTEICO flex 036 wood fibre, wall U ≤ 0.15
  6. Stud wallsTimber studs that carry the lining and services
  7. Primary frameGalvanized steel, bolted, so it unbolts and is reused
  8. Interior liningSolid timber surfaces
  9. Fit-outWet core, composting toilet, kitchen, safe pod
  10. Floor cassettesKingspan GreenGuard GG25-LG insulation, with the 900 L water tank inside
  11. Screw pilesNo concrete, removable. Pad footings where the ground needs them

It runs itself

Sun, rain and fresh air, used and reused on site.

PowerClean waterGreywater

The safe pod

The bed sits on a raised platform. Inside the platform is a sealed emergency store with enough to keep two people going for about two weeks if power, water or the road fails. It opens from inside, even in the dark.

Water and food

Two sealed 20 L water bladders and a gravity filter that also cleans tank or snow water. Two weeks of shelf-stable food, swapped once a year.

Heat and light

Two sleeping bags rated to −30 °C, thermal blankets and heat packs. Headlamps, a lantern, and a glow strip that shows where the pod is in a blackout.

Power and contact

A 1 kWh portable power station with a folding 200 W panel, a crank and solar radio, a satellite messenger, and spare batteries for the CO and smoke alarms.

Care and tools

First aid kit and spare medicines, documents in a waterproof pouch, a bucket toilet kit, a fire extinguisher, a multi-tool, tape, cord and a tarp.

Each drawer is labelled and colour-coded. A checklist inside the lid gets a quick check every season and a refresh every year.

Specifications

Floor area24.94 m²: a 16.12 m² module (3.1 × 5.2 m) and an 8.82 m² module (2.1 × 4.2 m) on a 5.2 × 5.2 m footprint. Combine them up to 41.06 m²

WallsKingspan QuadCore AWP insulated wall panel (LEC core) outside the steel frame, 100 mm STEICO flex 036 wood fibre between studs, U ≤ 0.15

WaterAbout 80 L a day for two. Rain with first flush to a Kingspan Slimline tank outside (drained in deep winter), then a custom flat 900 L store inside the warm floor that never freezes. 5 µm and carbon filter, UV lamp, greywater to plants. A water kiosk or snow melt tops up where rain is not enough
ToiletComposting toilet: no water, no sewer, compost for the soil

Questions

How accurate is the price?

The designer uses typical factory-direct prices for every material, fitting and system, plus transport and setup. It is a planning estimate. Your quote is a fixed price for your exact design.

What is not included?

Land, permits, site clearing, access for trucks and a crane, import duties and local taxes. The designer shows transport for the distance you enter.

Do I need planning permission?

It depends on where you build. Homes under about 25 m² have simpler rules in many places, but always check with your local authority before you order.

Can it really run off-grid?

Yes. The designer sizes solar, battery and water storage to your household and shows how many days you can go without sun or rain. The sealed backup hearth covers the coldest, cloudiest weeks, and the safe pod under the bed keeps you going if everything else stops.

Is it really wheelchair accessible?

The wheelchair version is. It keeps 80 cm paths, a 1.5 m turning circle in the living area and bathroom, a roll-in shower and a 1 m door, and the designer checks all of it as you change things. Our main render has a raised sleeping platform and a compact shower room, which are not wheelchair-friendly. Because the floor sits on screw piles, step-free entry needs a ramp or a platform lift, both offered.

Can homes be joined or stacked?

Wings bolt to the central module, and the stackable frame option is built for up to four storeys. Ask in your quote request.

Can I save or share my design?

Yes. Your design is kept in your browser, and you can download it as a file or copy a code to send to someone.

Design your home in ten minutes

No sign-up. Your design stays in your browser until you send it.
